item.title: About Me
item.description:
Hi, I’m Corin.

I love to learn, and to use that knowledge to build things and solve problems. I believe that everyone has a unique perspective on the world and deserves empathy, and that if we all put some more effort into understanding a bit more about the world and each other we would be better off.

I was born in Schenectady New York and grew up in Jonesboro Maine, where my family moved shortly after I was born. Nestled into the woods along the tidal Chandler River, my parents spared me from having any other chores as long as I moved firewood from where they dumped it by our driveway around back to our wood shed and stacked it neatly through the summer so we could stay warm in the winter. The river went out with the ocean and revealed entire ecosystems, only to be hidden again a few hours later with the tides, changing slightly every cycle.

item.title: Accelerated STEM Coaching
item.description:
Hi, I’m Corin.

I provide targeted, 1-on-1 remote coaching in AP Calculus, AP Physics, Computer Science, and Advanced Math.

My goal isn’t just to help students memorize formulas to pass next week’s exam—it’s to help them build deep, structural intuition for how these concepts work so they can solve complex problems independently.

How I Approach Teaching

Most STEM anxiety comes from treating math and physics like a list of arbitrary rules to memorize. When a concept feels abstract, it becomes exhausting.

item.title: Design / Build Portfolio
item.description:
Since 2016, I worked on numerous build projects. My involvement has included carpentry, design, and project management work. Some projects have been highly collaborative, some have been solo endeavors. This is an incomplete list of selected projects from my portfolio.

Structural Repair, Essex Vermont

While working for a contractor based out of Shelburne, Vermont, I did a mix of carpentry, project management, and business development work. One of my projects was leading a structural repair at a log cabin in Essex, Vermont. We and the client’s agreed that we wanted to open up the dining room into the main living space to improve circulation and light. However, when we demoed the wall, we found that the beam supporting the second floor was not continuous, and was split over the three studs seen in the image above near the bottom of the stairs. This unfortunately meant that much of the load from the second floor was getting transferred to the triple floor joist adjacent to the stairs, which was inadequate and beginning to deflect, and also meant that we couldn’t open up the room without further work.

item.title: Education Background
item.description:
Both of my parent’s are educators, so I have always been emersed in that world, and always valued the importance of lifelong learning.

Tutoring and Conservation Education

My first foray into teaching was working as a math, physics, computer sciene, and writing tutor while in high school at the Maine School of Science and Mathematics in Limestone, Maine. I did this for three years, my senior year serving as a Lead Tutor.
